item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Aarav looks at the diagram: a flat arrangement of six rectangles labelled $A$–$F$.

Which claim correctly decides whether this arrangement is a valid net for a cuboid?

options.A: It is a valid net: the six faces fold into a cuboid with no overlaps, and joining flaps are not counted as extra faces.
options.B: Call it a net even when the faces cannot meet edge-to-edge when folded from paper or cardboard.
options.C: Accept it as a net only because it has six regions, even if some faces would overlap when folded.
options.D: Call it a net only because the word net is the most obvious printed label near the diagram.
